qa.q: What did Lalremsiami call Damini's poem in the group?
What did Damini feel while typing and deleting messages in the group?
qa.a: Angry and hurt. Damini kept typing and stopping, which suggests an urge to blast back followed by a pause.

qa.q: What did Damini do that worked well here?

passage:
Last month in our friends' group, Jahnavi wrote, "Afreen always acts like she's the smartest person in the room, it's exhausting." Twelve people saw it. Somebody replied with a laughing sticker.
My whole face burned. I typed back something vicious about her grades and her copying my notes all term. I had my thumb on send. I wanted her to feel what I felt, in front of everyone.
Then I thought about how that message would live forever in everyone's screenshots. So I put the phone down and walked around the building twice.
Later, I messaged her privately: "What you wrote in the group really hurt me. If something I did bothered you, I'd rather hear it from you directly."
She called me that night. She'd been annoyed that I corrected her in class. We sorted it out, mostly. And nobody has a screenshot of me being cruel.

qa.q: How many people saw Jahnavi's message?
How did Afreen feel when she read Jahnavi's message?
qa.a: Afreen felt humiliated and furious, her face burning, and wanted to hurt Jahnavi back in front of everyone.
Pausing, then messaging Jahnavi privately about the hurt led to an honest call instead of a public fight everyone could screenshot.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi have felt when Afreen messaged privately?
qa.a: Jahnavi probably felt surprised and a bit guilty, which made it easier for her to call and explain why she was annoyed.

grounding: A teen hurt by a friend's harsh group message pauses, takes it to a private chat and says what hurt instead of retaliating publicly.

passage:
Hockey coach's note, girls' under-16, Saturday
After practice, Noor sat on the bench looking at her phone, jaw tight. I asked if she was alright. She showed me: in the team chat, Amandeep had written that Noor "hogs the ball and cries when she doesn't score."
Noor said she was about to reply with something about Amandeep's missed penalties, "so everyone sees." She had it typed.
I didn't take her phone. I asked what she wanted to happen after she sent it. She thought, then said, "I want her to know it hurt. Not a war."
I suggested she wait until she felt calmer and send Amandeep a private message instead. She deleted the draft. Twenty minutes later she wrote: "Your message in the group hurt. Can we talk before Monday's practice?"
Amandeep replied quickly and apologised. I will speak to the whole team on Monday about how we use the group chat.

qa.q: What did Amandeep write about Noor in the team chat?
qa.a: That Noor "hogs the ball and cries when she doesn't score."

qa.q: What was Noor feeling when the note-writer found her on the bench?
qa.a: She felt angry and hurt, jaw tight, and wanted to blast Amandeep back in front of the team.

qa.q: How did the note-writer help Noor choose a better response?
qa.a: By asking what she wanted to happen, which helped her see she wanted Amandeep to know it hurt, and suggesting a private message.

qa.q: How might Amandeep see Noor's private message?
qa.a: Amandeep seems to realise her comment hurt and feels sorry, since she replied quickly and apologised.

grounding: A teen hurt by a teammate's harsh group comment pauses, takes it to a private message and says what hurt, as a coach observes.
